Class OrificeFlowMeter

java.lang.Object
neqsim.util.NamedBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.MeasurementDeviceBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.StreamMeasurementDeviceBaseClass
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.DifferentialPressureFlowMeter
neqsim.process.measurementdevice.OrificeFlowMeter
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, TransientStateParticipant<DifferentialPressureFlowMeter.DifferentialPressureFlowMeterState>, MeasurementDeviceInterface, ProcessElementInterface, NamedInterface
public class OrificeFlowMeter extends DifferentialPressureFlowMeter
Orifice-plate differential-pressure flow meter following ISO 5167-1 and ISO 5167-2.

The discharge coefficient is the Reader-Harris/Gallagher (1998) equation, ISO 5167-2:2022 Formula (4): 

 C = 0.5961 + 0.0261 beta^2 - 0.216 beta^8
     + 0.000521 (1e6 beta / ReD) ^ 0.7
     + (0.0188 + 0.0063 A) beta^3.5 (1e6 / ReD) ^ 0.3
     + (0.043 + 0.080 exp(-10 L1) - 0.123 exp(-7 L1)) (1 - 0.11 A) beta^4 / (1 - beta^4)
     - 0.031 (M2' - 0.8 M2'^1.1) beta^1.3

with A = (19000 beta / ReD) ^ 0.8, M2' = 2 L2' / (1 - beta), and where D < 71.12 mm the additional term 0.011 (0.75 - beta) (2.8 - D / 25.4) (D in millimetres) is added. L1 and L2' depend on the OrificeFlowMeter.TappingArrangement: both zero for corner tappings, 1 and 0.47 for D and D/2 tappings, and 25.4 / D (millimetres) for flange tappings.

The expansibility factor is ExpansibilityModel.ORIFICE. Both C and epsilon are only valid within the ISO 5167-2 limits of use: 12.5 mm <= d, 50 mm <= D <= 1000 mm, 0.1 <= beta <= 0.75, and a Reynolds-number range that depends on the tapping arrangement and beta; see getValidityViolations().

Wet-gas operation (ISO/TR 11583)

Selecting OrificeFlowMeter.WetGasCorrelation.ISO_TR_11583 switches the device to the ISO/TR 11583 Clause 7 wet-gas orifice method. Unlike the Venturi tube (ISO/TR 11583 Clause 6), the discharge coefficient is never replaced: clause 7.5.2 states that C remains the plain Reader-Harris/Gallagher equation, evaluated at the Reynolds number that would be obtained if only the gas were flowing. The gas mass flow rate becomes 

 qm,gas = C / sqrt(1 - beta ^ 4) * epsilon * (pi / 4) * d ^ 2 * sqrt(2 * dP * rho1,gas) / Phi

with the same Chisholm-form over-reading equation as the Venturi tube, Phi = sqrt(1 + CCh X + X^2), CCh = (rho,liquid / rho1,gas)^n + (rho1,gas / rho,liquid)^n, but the orifice's own exponent (ISO/TR 11583 Equation (6a)/(6b)), which depends only on the gas densiometric Froude number and has no diameter-ratio term: 

 n = 0.214                                    for 0.2 <= Fr,gas < 1.5
 n = (1 / sqrt(2) - 0.3 / sqrt(Fr,gas)) ^ 2    for Fr,gas > 1.5

The liquid load is supplied either as an absolute rate (setLiquidMassFlowRate(double, String)), as a liquid-to-gas mass ratio (setLiquidToGasMassRatio(double)), or taken from the phase split of the connected stream (setLiquidFromStream(boolean)). When the liquid rate is unknown and 0.5 <= beta <= 0.68, ISO/TR 11583 7.5.5 allows X to be derived from the permanent pressure loss measured at a third tapping 5D to 7D downstream of the plate; see setPressureLoss(double, String).

Limitations of ISO/TR 11583 Clause 7. The equations were derived for nitrogen, natural gas, Exxsol D80 and decane and may not apply to significantly different liquids. Limits of use: 0.24 <= beta <= 0.73, 0 < X <= 0.3, Fr,gas >= 0.2, rho,gas / rho,liquid > 0.014, D >= 50 mm; the pressure-loss route additionally requires 0.5 <= beta <= 0.68 and two density-ratio-dependent bounds on X. Validity is reported by getValidityViolations() rather than enforced.

      public void setPressureLoss(double pressureLoss, String unit)
      Sets the permanent pressure loss measured between the upstream tapping and a third tapping 5D to 7D downstream of the plate. When set, and no liquid load has been supplied, the Lockhart-Martinelli parameter is derived from the pressure-loss ratio using ISO/TR 11583 7.5.5.
      Parameters:
      pressureLoss - permanent pressure loss, must be non-negative
      unit - pressure unit, one of "Pa", "kPa", "MPa", "bar", "mbar" or "psi"

    • solveWetGas

      private OrificeFlowMeter.WetGasResult solveWetGas()
      Returns the wet-gas evaluation for the current operating point, reusing the last solve when nothing that buildWetGasSignature() tracks has changed. Every wet-gas getter and getMassFlowRatePerSecond() go through this method, so multiple reads within the same timestep see one consistent, cheaply-repeated result instead of re-running the iterative solve on every call.
      Returns:
      the wet-gas evaluation outcome

    • buildWetGasSignature

      private double[] buildWetGasSignature()
      Builds a cheap fingerprint of every input computeWetGas() depends on (stream properties and wet-gas configuration), used by solveWetGas() to detect whether a fresh solve is required. Unset optional inputs (e.g. pressureLoss) are NaN; Arrays.equals(double[], double[]) treats NaN as equal to NaN (per its Javadoc contract), so that does not defeat the cache.
      Returns:
      fingerprint array, compared with Arrays.equals(double[], double[])

    • computeWetGas

      private OrificeFlowMeter.WetGasResult computeWetGas()
      Solves the ISO/TR 11583 Clause 7 wet-gas equations for the current operating point. Returns the dry-gas result (from the base class's Reynolds-number iteration) when no wet-gas correlation is selected or when no liquid load is available. Never throws.
      Returns:
      the wet-gas evaluation outcome

    • calcChisholmExponent

      private double calcChisholmExponent(double froude)
      Calculates the ISO/TR 11583 Clause 7 exponent n from the gas densiometric Froude number. Below the 0.2 lower bound of the correlation the 0.214 plateau is extrapolated rather than returning NaN, so the meter never throws; the point is reported by getValidityViolations() instead.
      Parameters:
      froude - gas densiometric Froude number [-]
      Returns:
      exponent n [-]
